spans.s:
Andhra is the name of a people, and is mentioned with the Puṇḍras, Śabaras, Pulindas, and Mūtibas, as being the outcasts resulting from the refusal of the fifty eldest sons of viśvāmitra to accept his adoption of śunaḥśepa. It may fairly be deduced from this statement that these people were recognized as nonAryan, as the Andhras certainly seem to have been.
Foot notes aitareya brāhmaṇa, vii. 18; śāṅkhāyana śrauta sūtra, xv. 26, where instead of udāntyaḥ (‘beyond the borders’) the reading is udañcaḥ (‘northern’), but the former is obviously correct. The Sāṅkhāyana omits the Pulindas, and has Mūcīpas.
Vincent Smith, Zeitschrift der Deutschen Morgenländischen Gesellschaft, 56, 657 et seq., who places them originally in Eastern India between the Kṛṣṇā and Godāvarī rivers; cf. Rapson, Catalogue of Indian Coins, xv., xvi.; Bhandarkar, Bombay Gazetteer, 1. ii. 138.
